standard.title: Create and edit literary texts with sustained voice
standard.description: create and edit literary texts with a sustained 'voice', selecting and adapting text structures, literary devices, and language, auditory and visual features for purposes and audiences
standard.prior_knowledge: Students create and edit literary texts including hybrids (AC9E9LE06). They have not yet created and edited literary texts with a sustained voice, deliberately selecting and adapting text structures, literary devices and multimodal features for specific purposes and audiences.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create and edit literary texts with a sustained voice, selecting and adapting text structures, literary devices, and language, auditory and visual features for purposes and audiences.

nodes.label: Constructing and sustaining a voice
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can construct a deliberate authorial voice in a literary text and sustain it across the text through consistent language and structural choices.
nodes.minimum_width: Create a short literary text with a clearly constructed voice — evidenced by consistent language register, tone and perspective choices — and sustain it across the whole piece.
nodes.typical_width: Create a literary text with a sustained voice, using deliberate language, structural and literary device choices to construct and maintain a consistent authorial persona, register and perspective.
wider: Experiment with a range of voice types across different short texts (e.g. collective voice, unreliable narrator, protest voice) to develop fluency with voice construction
Create a suite of short texts on the same key idea expressed in different voices, comparing how voice shapes what can be said and how
Experiment with First Nations Australian authorial voice conventions in a short piece, reflecting on the choices made and their cultural significance
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires students to select and adapt text structures for a sustained voice — without a functional understanding of how voice is constructed and maintained, structural and device choices in Node 2 have no coherent purpose to serve.

response_modes.reason: Students who only attempt one voice type may produce technically correct but thin voice construction; experimenting with multiple voice types builds genuine understanding of how voice is constructed rather than accidentally achieved.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Voice construction is rich when students can experiment across voice types and purposes — the suite-of-texts task and voice contrast offer genuine creative depth for advancing students.
success_criteria: Creates a literary text with a discernible and consistent authorial voice
Can identify the specific language or structural choices that construct and sustain the voice

nodes.label: Selecting and adapting text structures and literary devices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select and adapt text structures and literary devices for a specific purpose and audience, explaining their choices.
nodes.minimum_width: In a literary text, make and describe at least two deliberate choices of text structure or literary device for a specific purpose, with an explanation of the effect intended.
nodes.typical_width: Create and edit a literary text that demonstrates deliberate selection and adaptation of text structures, literary devices, and language and visual features for a specific purpose and audience, with reflection on choices made.
wider: Experiment with adapting aesthetic features encountered in mentor texts into own writing, explaining what was borrowed and how it was adapted
Create a literary text for a specific real audience (school community, competition) and reflect on how purpose and audience shaped every structural and device choice
Create a literary text that incorporates or responds to a First Nations Australian text, reflecting on the choices required to do so responsibly
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 3 (editing) requires students to evaluate and revise their structural and device choices — without having made deliberate choices in Node 2, there is nothing purposeful to edit or reflect on.

response_modes.reason: Students need to develop the habit of reasoning from purpose and audience backward to structural and device choices — moving from 'I want to create X effect' to 'therefore I will use Y structure/device'; this reasoning chain is the core capability move here.

success_criteria: Makes at least two deliberate choices of text structure or literary device for a specific purpose
Can explain the intended effect of each choice on the intended audience

nodes.label: Editing and reflecting on literary craft choices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can edit their literary texts to refine voice and craft, describing choices made and reflecting on the effect of those choices on the text.
nodes.minimum_width: Edit a literary text by making at least two revisions to improve voice consistency or craft, and describe what was changed and why.
nodes.typical_width: Edit and refine a literary text, revising choices of structure, literary devices and language features to strengthen voice and purpose; reflect on how choices may be developed further.
wider: Share a literary text with a peer reader and use their response to guide a further editing round, reflecting on how reader feedback informs craft decisions
Produce a writer's commentary alongside a literary text, documenting the editing process and reflecting on how each revision strengthened the text
Compare two drafts of the same piece and analyse specifically what editing decisions improved the voice and craft

response_modes.reason: Editing integrates all the craft elements from nodes 1–2 — sustained voice, structure, device choices — into a coherent whole; the editing phase is where students demonstrate they can coordinate all elements rather than managing each in isolation.

success_criteria: Makes at least two revisions to a literary text with a stated reason for each change
Reflects on how at least one revision improved the voice, structure or device choices
